card.name: Subject right before "can occur" in opioid warnings
card.fires_on: The word just before "can occur" or "can lead to" in boxed-warning text about opioid addiction and GI bleeding. It marks the subject (Addiction, which, These events) waiting for its verb.

modes.label: Addiction starting a sentence
modes.description: The word Addiction opens a sentence right after a statement that addiction risk is unknown in appropriately prescribed patients.

modes.label: Which after misuse risks
modes.description: The word which follows the list of addiction, abuse and misuse and leads into a result clause.
modes.example: Because the use of XTAMPZA ER exposes patients and other users to the risks of opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse,<< which>> can lead to overdose and death, assess

modes.label: Can after These events
modes.description: The word can follows "These events" in the NSAID GI bleeding warning.

card.writes: It promotes linking verbs like "is" and "are", so it pushes the model toward a verb following the subject.
card.plain: It fires on the subject word of a warning sentence, just before the verb saying the harm can occur.
